text:
Elaine R.: Compliance asked for 24 months of SIEM exports (alerts, auth events, flow logs). Our export pipeline currently retains 90d. Can eng-security outline safe options, RBAC implications, and KMS concerns for cross-account access? CC @Zia P.

Kevin M.: Quick thoughts — create a long-term archive (LTA) S3 bucket with lifecycle to Glacier/Deep Archive, SSE-KMS (alias/siem-archive), enable bucket logging + versioning. Cross-account read via an explicit IAM role in consumer account and a narrow KMS key policy granting kms:Decrypt to that role. Note: KMS key rotation + bad key policy = broken access, so plan rotation carefully.

Ash K.: +1 to LTA. Prefer adding a re-encryption or access-proxy in our account rather than broad KMS grants to external accounts. Also consider STS-based JIT access (short-lived creds) and audit every assume-role event. For compliance evidence we can ship signed manifests with SHA256 checksums.

security-bot: [automated] exporter-service alert: spike in 503 errors at 2026-07-16T10:12Z during archive writes. Incident INC-2026-07 opened and assigned to eng-infra.

Zia P.: Security notes:
- Larger retention increases blast radius; restrict LTA reads to a dedicated group 'siem-archive-read' and require MFA + SSO session <=1h.
- Don't grant kms:* to external accounts. If external consumer *must* have a key, use a re-encryption flow: our CMK decrypts, proxy re-encrypts into consumer CMK.
- Enable S3 access logs + object-level audit and keep read/audit logs for 2y as well.

Elaine R.: Can we get a short options list I can send to compliance? Also confirm GDPR/PIPEDA implications if auditors request raw PII-containing logs.

Kevin M.: I'll draft a PR with three options and tradeoffs:
1) Fast (1 week): S3 LTA in our account + SSE-KMS (our CMK) + cross-account key policy granting decrypt to consumer role. Pros: fastest. Cons: cross-account key exposure, rotation complexity.
2) Balanced (2-3 weeks): LTA + re-encryption proxy + strict RBAC + JIT STS for reads. Pros: lower key exposure, better auditability. Cons: more infra + cost.
3) Cleanest (onboarding time varies): Upload-to-customer-bucket pattern where consumer provides bucket and CMK; we push encrypted exports into their bucket via a limited-role. Pros: cryptographic separation. Cons: legal/ops onboarding overhead.

Sample IAM trust snippet I'll include in PR:
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::999999999999:role/siem-consumer-reader"},
    "Action": "sts:AssumeRole",
    "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"sts:ExternalId": "audit-2026-06"}}
  }]
}
```

And a simple S3 lifecycle rule example:
```json
{
  "Rules": [{
    "ID": "move-to-deep-archive",
    "Status": "Enabled",
    "Filter": {},
    "Transitions": [{"Days": 90, "StorageClass": "GLACIER"}, {"Days": 365, "StorageClass": "DEEP_ARCHIVE"}]
  }]
}
```

Ash K.: I'll own the JIT RBAC design and the re-encryption proxy spec. I'll also add the exporter container vulnerability scan to the checklist before enabling LTA.

Zia P.: From security: prefer option 2. Will provide a short review in 24h. Also: require object-level integrity metadata (SHA256) and sign manifests with a key we rotate on a scheduled cadence. :white_check_mark:

Elaine R.: Action items:
- Kevin: PR for option 1 prototype (due EOD Thu)
- Ash: JIT RBAC design doc + proxy spec (share by Mon)
- Zia: security review + compliance note (24h)
- Eng-infra: follow up on INC-2026-07 and confirm exporter stability

Thanks all — I'll add results to the audit package once we have PR + design.
